0: Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia Vehicle Policy
1: The purpose of this policy is to set forth the guidelines under which vehicles owned or leased by the Town of Pine Mountain may be operated and used.
2:
The provisions of this policy apply to all Town employees who operate and/or use Town vehicles. As part of a Department’s standard operating procedures, a Department Head may choose to adopt rules of operation and use that are more stringent (but not less) than those this policy outlines.

It is the policy of the Town of Pine Mountain to authorize the acquisition and utilization of vehicles for use by employees of the Town, in the conduct of their employment responsibilities, either during the work shift or on a twenty-four (24) hour on-call basis. Town vehicles are for use by Town employees on Town related business only.

Town vehicles are assigned on a departmental basis to be used by that Department only. Other departments are not to use vehicles not assigned to them unless given permission by the Department which has primary possession of such vehicle.

They are not personal vehicles and are not for personal use. Town vehicles should be viewed as belonging to the citizens of Pine Mountain and are assigned solely for purposes consistent with providing services to those citizens.

When Town vehicles are not on Town business, they are to be parked at the appropriate Town Department office so that they will be available for official Town use. Such office or location shall be determined by which Town department has possession or use of such vehicle.
3:
- l. Town vehicles must have the Town seal or department insignia patches affixed on the drivers and passenger side doors (except for unmarked Police vehicles), and may only be used for legitimate municipal business.

- 2. Town vehicles will not be used to transport passengers who are not guests of the Town or are otherwise directly or indirectly related to Town business. Passengers should be limited to Town employees and those individuals who are guests of the Town

and/or are directly associated with Town work activity (committee members, consultants, contractors, municipal employees from other communities, or by others that have been granted special permission of the department head).

- 3. Personal property should in no case be left in Town vehicles which should contain only those items for which the vehicle is designed. The Town shall not be liable for the loss or damage of any personal property transported in the vehicle.

4, Employees are expected to keep Town vehicles clean, and to report any malfunction or damage to their supervisor immediately.

- 5. Employees are not allowed to transport animals in Town vehicles unless they are service animals or such transport is a job related function.

- 6. Employees and authorized passengers are not allowed to smoke in Town vehicles. 7. Employees and authorized passengers must wear seatbelts in Town vehicles so equipped during operation of the vehicle (except for Police who must respond to an incident where the use of a seat belt may present an unsafe situation for the vehicle operator and/or occupant).

- 8. Employees are not to use cell phones while driving Town vehicles except in cases of emergency response. No texts may be made or answered.

- 9. Employees shall not operate Town vehicles under the influence of alcohol, illegal drugs, or prescription drugs or medication that may interfere with effective and safe operation of the vehicle.

- 10. Employees who operate Town vehicles must have a valid motor vehicle license issued by the state of their current residence and may be required to provide proof of valid motor vehicle license once every six (6) months.

- 11. Employees driving Town vehicles shall obey all applicable traffic and parking regulations, ordinances, and laws.

- a) Employees who incur parking or other traffic fines in Town vehicles will generally be personally responsible for payment of such fines unless the Department Head approves the payment of such fines by the Town.

- b) Employees who are issued citations for any offense while using a Town vehicle must notify their supervisor immediately when practicable, but in no case later than 24 hours. Failure to provide such notice may be grounds for disciplinary action

up to and including termination.

- 9) An employee who is assigned a Town vehicle and who is arrested for or charged with a motor vehicle offense for which the punishment includes suspension or revocation of his or her motor vehicle operator’s license, (whether in his or her personal vehicle or in a Town vehicle), must notify his or her supervisor no later than the beginning of their next work shift. Conviction for such an offense may be grounds for loss of municipal vehicle privileges and/or further disciplinary action up to and including termination.

- d) An employee who is involved in any motor vehicle accident involving a Town vehicle shall contact their supervisor immediately who will contact the Police.

- 12. No employee may use a Town vehicle for out of state use without advance approval of the Department Head.

- 13. Employees using Town vehicles shall fuel same at the gasoline tank the Town maintains for that purpose unless refueling is required while out of town on official Town business. All periodic, preventative maintenance and necessary repairs to Town vehicles shall be performed by outside contractors approved by the Town Council.

Failure to comply with any and all provisions of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including removal of Town vehicle privileges, suspension, and/or termination employment.

ASSIGNMENT OF TOWN VEHICLES FOR 24 HOUR USE (VEHICLE APPROVED FOR COMMUTING PURPOSES)

- 1. The assignment of vehicles for twenty-four (24) hour use will be made in writing by Department Heads and will only be considered for employees who require a vehicle for the ordinary and necessary discharge of their job functions. Criteria, which will be used in the determination of eligibility for 24-hour vehicle use, include:

. officially designated on-call status; . requirement for frequent emergency availability; ° emergency or other equipment contained in the vehicle;

Such assignment may be rescinded with reasonable notice for work-related reasons.

- 2. When commuting, Town vehicle use is limited to travel to and from the residence and place of work. Town vehicles should be driven over the most direct route taking into account road and traffic conditions. The vehicle should not be utilized for travel outside a direct commuting route for personal reasons.

- 3. Whenever a position becomes vacant, the authorization for 24-hour use for commuting shall be reevaluated.

4, Employees assigned vehicles for 24-hour use involving a lengthy commute time may, in the discretion of their supervisor, be required to reimburse the Town for the additional operational or maintenance cost as determined by the Town Council.

- 5. Employees assigned Town vehicles on a 24-hour basis will be given a copy of this policy and will be required to sign a confirmation of receipt.

Driving Emergency Vehicle Standard Operating Procedure
4:
Scope: This policy is to establish a basic guide to be followed when driving an emergency vehicle. The said emergency vehicle shall consist of any vehicle owned and operated by the Town of Pine Mountain and any vehicle owned and operated by other local agencies that have entrusted the membership of the Pine Mountain Fire Department personnel to operate. SAFETY IS OF THE UPMOST IMPORTANCE

Responsibilities: Each member of the Pine Mountain Fire Department shall follow the established guidelines when operating an emergency vehicle.

Effective Date: This policy shall replace any and all previous policies pertaining to the driving of emergency vehicles and shall be effective as of February 9, 2015.

Definitions: ETA-Estimated Time of Arrival; IC-Incident Command; OIC-Officer in Charge; TAC-Tactical Channel or other fire ground channel.

Age Restriction: No one under the age of 21 years shall be permitted to operate any fire department vehicle responding to an emergency.

Driving Emergency Vehicles: While it is understood that emergency vehicles need to arrive on the scene of an emergency as quickly as possible, they must be operated in a safe manner. The following guidelines govern the driving of emergency vehicles:

I) No one shall be allowed to drive a fire department vehicle unless they have a valid Georgia Drivers License as required for the particular fire department vehicle. A copy of the firefighter’s license shall be on file with the fire department and/or Pine Mountain Town Hall.

A) At a minimum, a Georgia Class F non-commercial driver’s license or higher-class driver's license is required to drive fire engines owned and/or operated by the Pine Mountain Fire Department.

B) Holders of a Georgia Class FP non-commercial driver’s license will be allowed to drive a fire engine but only if they are accompanied by someone with a Georgia Class F non-commercial license or higher class license.

I[} Seat belts and other restraining devices will be used by all persons operating or being transported inside a fire department vehicle.

Ill) While enroute to non-emergency situations, emergency lights, siren, air horn, or other emergency signaling device will not be used. A) During non-emergency situations fire department vehicles will not be operated in an emergency manner.

B) Non-emergency situations include, but are not limited to: tree(s) or tree limb(s) across a roadway during good visibility, animal rescue, transport of water during non-emergency

situations, any other situation deemed non-emergency by the Fire Chief, IC, OIC, or the 911 center.

- 1) When responding non-emergency, the IC or OIC will advise the 911 center of the fire department's non-emergency response.

- 2) Upon arrival on the non-emergency scene, emergency lighting will be activated to warn passersby and to protect fire department personnel.

iV) During emergency situations, the emergency lights will be activated and audible alarming devices will be operated in accordance with state laws.

A) The 911 center will be advised of the emergency response as each emergency vehicle leaves the station and will be advised as each emergency vehicle arrives at the scene.

B) When using emergency warning devices, visual and/or audible, remember the following:

- 1) Such use does not give the responding vehicle the right-of-way. 2) Always stop and/or yield when approaching an intersection.

- 3) Be careful with the air horn usage as not to deplete the air supply that operates the air brakes.

C) Regardless of the siren sound that is used while responding, state laws require the sound be changed or alternated within 200’ of any intersection.

D) As an added safety precaution, if an emergency vehicle is so equipped, the air horns should be activated when approaching an intersection or slower traffic.

E) During emergency response both emergency lights and siren are to be operating while moving.

E) The siren and radios should be operated by the IC or OIC.

V) Always use the parking brake and place wheel chocks when a fire department vehicle is stopped and left unattended.

VI) If you and the emergency vehicle are involved in an accident, follow these guidelines. Both you and the apparatus are completely out of service. Activate any emergency lights that remain operable on the vehicle, provided such activation does not result in a threat of fire and/or explosion. Set the apparatus parking brake. Notify 911 of the accident and location. Check for and report any injuries. Have 911 notify law enforcement (Sheriff's Office and/or State Patrol), the fire chief, and city officials.

Failure to Comply: If this policy for driving an emergency vehicle is violated the penalty will be, but not limited to:

First Offense: Verbal warming about the offense

Second Offense: Driving privileges suspended for 30 days

Third Offense: Driving privileges suspended for 6 months

Fourth Offense: Termination with the Pine Mountain Fire Department
